pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR fixes that date overrides of fixed hosts are taken into account for round-robin events. This prevents round-robin events being booked where the fixed hosts are unavailable. 

This PR also fixes that date overrides didn't adjust to different timezones. If the organizer has a date override from 10-11 UTC it always showed the slots from 10-11 open no matter what timezone the attendee has.

Fixes #8207
Fixes #8329

Fixes: #8273

**Environment**: Staging(main branch) / Production

## Type of change

- Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How should this be tested?

**Date overrides for fixed hosts (round-robin):** 
- Create a round-robin event with one fixed host and host round-robin host
- Create a date override for fixed host (round-robin host should also be available at that time)
- Check available slots of event on the day of the date override, it should only show the slots where fixed host is available
- Test that with different time zones on booking page and on the availabilities of fixed and round-robin host

**Date override timezones issue:** 
- Create a date override 
- Go to the booking page of a personal event 
- Change the timezone to a different one that the availability with the date override is 
- See the available slots of the day with the date override change accordingly 
- Also test with different timezones here
pr.title: Date override fixes

raw_findings.body: The function returns true before ever running the `busy.every(...)` loop, so already-booked/busy times on override days are offered as available and can be double-booked.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Availability computation reports busy slots as free, allowing conflicting bookings.
raw_findings.impact: The function returns true before ever running the `busy.every(...)` loop, so already-booked/busy times on override days are offered as available and can be double-booked.
raw_findings.root_cause: New override handling returns availability directly rather than only deciding the working-hours dimension and delegating the busy check to the existing logic.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not return early; when the slot falls inside the override window, fall through to the existing busy-time evaluation (`return busy.every(...)`) instead of returning true.
raw_findings.title: Date override day short-circuits busy-time checking
raw_findings.trigger: A host has a date override for a given day and already has an accepted booking / calendar busy block inside that override window; a slot overlapping that busy block is evaluated by checkIfIsAvailable.

raw_findings.body: `find` returns the 13:00-17:00 entry because the slot is outside it, so the whole check returns false and a slot that is inside the 09:00-12:00 range is wrongly filtered out of the schedule.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Valid bookable slots disappear for hosts with split daily availability.
raw_findings.impact: `find` returns the 13:00-17:00 entry because the slot is outside it, so the whole check returns false and a slot that is inside the 09:00-12:00 range is wrongly filtered out of the schedule.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new check uses an "any entry excludes" predicate instead of an "at least one entry includes" predicate over a list of disjoint working-hour ranges.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Invert the predicate: treat the slot as inside working hours when `workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)` and only return false when no entry covers it.
raw_findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slot if any single working-hour entry excludes it
raw_findings.trigger: A host schedule has more than one availability range covering the same weekday (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), producing two WorkingHours entries with the same day; a 10:00 slot is checked.

raw_findings.body: `end` equals `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition can never detect a slot that overruns the working-hour boundary, and slots extending past the end of availability are accepted.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Boundary-overrunning slots pass the newly added working-hours validation, defeating its purpose.
raw_findings.impact: `end` equals `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition can never detect a slot that overruns the working-hour boundary, and slots extending past the end of availability are accepted.
raw_findings.root_cause: Copy-paste of the start-time expression when computing the slot end offset.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compute `const end = slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute();` (handling day rollover) so the slot end is compared against `workingHour.endTime`.
raw_findings.title: Slot end minute computed from slot start time in working-hours check
raw_findings.trigger: A slot starts shortly before the end of the host's working hours, e.g. a 60-minute event starting at 16:30 when working hours end at 17:00.

raw_findings.body: `find` matches the 14:00-16:00 range (slot ends before its start), so the function returns false and the slot inside the 09:00-11:00 range is removed from the schedule.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Legitimate slots are dropped whenever a date has multiple override ranges.
raw_findings.impact: `find` matches the 14:00-16:00 range (slot ends before its start), so the function returns false and the slot inside the 09:00-11:00 range is removed from the schedule.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new override logic uses `find` for "some range excludes the slot" rather than aggregating all same-day ranges before deciding.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Determine availability with a positive predicate: mark the day as overridden, then return true only if `dateOverrides.some(range => slot fits inside range)`; return false only when no same-day range contains the slot.
raw_findings.title: Date-override check rejects a slot that falls outside any one of several same-day overrides
raw_findings.trigger: A host creates two ranges for the same date override (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00) and a slot at 09:30 is evaluated.

raw_findings.body: Two distinct Dayjs objects are never reference-equal, so this branch never executes; the intended "whole day blocked" short-circuit is dead code and the decision falls through to the subsequent range comparisons, which can classify the slot as available.
raw_findings.failure_mode: An intentionally added guard never triggers, silently changing availability semantics for zero-length overrides.
raw_findings.impact: Two distinct Dayjs objects are never reference-equal, so this branch never executes; the intended "whole day blocked" short-circuit is dead code and the decision falls through to the subsequent range comparisons, which can classify the slot as available.
raw_findings.root_cause: Object identity comparison used where a value/time comparison is required for Dayjs instances.
raw_findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === so the empty-override branch is dead
raw_findings.trigger: A date override marks the day as fully unavailable, producing an override whose start and end are the same instant.

raw_findings.body: `dayjs(date.start)...format()` renders in the server's local timezone while `slotStartTime` is a UTC dayjs, so the two day strings disagree and the override is either ignored (slots not restricted) or applied to the wrong day.
raw_findings.evidence:
dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") ===
        slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")
raw_findings.failure_mode: Availability differs between deployments depending on the server TZ setting; tests running in UTC hide the defect.
raw_findings.impact: `dayjs(date.start)...format()` renders in the server's local timezone while `slotStartTime` is a UTC dayjs, so the two day strings disagree and the override is either ignored (slots not restricted) or applied to the wrong day.
raw_findings.root_cause: New code parses the override Date without `.utc()`, making the day key dependent on the host process timezone.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `dayjs.utc(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` so both sides of the comparison are in UTC.
raw_findings.title: Override day matched using server-local formatting against a UTC slot day
raw_findings.trigger: The Node process runs with a non-UTC TZ (e.g. TZ=America/New_York) and an override starts near a day boundary in UTC.

raw_findings.body: `hour()`/`minute()` discard the day rollover, yielding startTime=1230 and endTime=30; buildSlots skips ranges where `start >= end`, so the override day shows no slots at all (or slots at the wrong clock time when both ends roll over).
raw_findings.evidence:
startTime:
          dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 +
          dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").minute(),
        endTime:
          dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 +
          dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").minute(),
raw_findings.failure_mode: Date overrides silently produce empty or misplaced availability for invitees in distant timezones.
raw_findings.impact: `hour()`/`minute()` discard the day rollover, yielding startTime=1230 and endTime=30; buildSlots skips ranges where `start >= end`, so the override day shows no slots at all (or slots at the wrong clock time when both ends roll over).
raw_findings.root_cause: The new invitee-offset adjustment is applied to a timestamp but then reduced to same-day minutes-since-midnight without handling day boundary crossings.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compute the shifted minutes as a signed offset from the invitee day start (e.g. diff in minutes against `startOfInviteeDay`) and clamp/split ranges that cross midnight instead of taking `hour()*60 + minute()`.
raw_findings.title: Timezone-shifted override loses day rollover, producing endTime before startTime
raw_findings.trigger: Organizer in Asia/Kolkata sets a date override 09:00-13:00 IST and the invitee views the page in America/Los_Angeles (offset difference about -12.5h), so the shifted start falls on the previous calendar day while the end stays on the same day.

raw_findings.body: `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the runtime's guessed timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed for the server/browser zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary wrong offset, showing overrides at incorrect times.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent timezone misalignment for callers that do not populate the new optional field.
raw_findings.impact: `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the runtime's guessed timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed for the server/browser zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary wrong offset, showing overrides at incorrect times.
raw_findings.root_cause: The added `timeZone` field on TimeRange is optional while the new offset computation assumes it is always provided.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either make `timeZone` required on the override input consumed by getSlots, or default explicitly, e.g. `.tz(override.timeZone ?? organizerTimeZone)`.
raw_findings.title: Optional override timeZone dereferenced without fallback in getSlots
raw_findings.trigger: Any getSlots caller that passes `dateOverrides` built from `TimeRange` values without the newly added optional `timeZone` field (the type declares `timeZone?: string`), e.g. team availability components or future callers.

raw_findings.failure_mode: Reviewers and CI cannot verify the change the PR is primarily about.

raw_findings.root_cause: New availability-filtering logic in checkIfIsAvailable was added without a corresponding scenario test for team/round-robin scheduling.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a getSchedule test with a ROUND_ROBIN event type having one fixed host with a date override and one always-available round-robin host, asserting only the fixed host's override window is returned.

validated_findings.body: The function returns true before ever running the `busy.every(...)` loop, so already-booked/busy times on override days are offered as available and can be double-booked.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Availability computation reports busy slots as free, allowing conflicting bookings.
validated_findings.impact: The function returns true before ever running the `busy.every(...)` loop, so already-booked/busy times on override days are offered as available and can be double-booked.
validated_findings.root_cause: New override handling returns availability directly rather than only deciding the working-hours dimension and delegating the busy check to the existing logic.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Do not return early; when the slot falls inside the override window, fall through to the existing busy-time evaluation (`return busy.every(...)`) instead of returning true.
validated_findings.title: Date override day short-circuits busy-time checking
validated_findings.trigger: A host has a date override for a given day and already has an accepted booking / calendar busy block inside that override window; a slot overlapping that busy block is evaluated by checkIfIsAvailable.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 133-135 shows `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` which returns before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153. When a slot falls within a date override window, the function returns true without checking busy times, allowing double-booking.

validated_findings.body: `find` returns the 13:00-17:00 entry because the slot is outside it, so the whole check returns false and a slot that is inside the 09:00-12:00 range is wrongly filtered out of the schedule.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Valid bookable slots disappear for hosts with split daily availability.
validated_findings.impact: `find` returns the 13:00-17:00 entry because the slot is outside it, so the whole check returns false and a slot that is inside the 09:00-12:00 range is wrongly filtered out of the schedule.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new check uses an "any entry excludes" predicate instead of an "at least one entry includes" predicate over a list of disjoint working-hour ranges.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Invert the predicate: treat the slot as inside working hours when `workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)` and only return false when no entry covers it.
validated_findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slot if any single working-hour entry excludes it
validated_findings.trigger: A host schedule has more than one availability range covering the same weekday (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), producing two WorkingHours entries with the same day; a 10:00 slot is checked.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 139-147 use `find` with a predicate that returns true when slot is OUTSIDE a working hour entry. With multiple entries for same day (e.g., 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), a 10:00 slot would match the 13:00-17:00 entry (outside it), causing false return and rejecting a valid slot.

validated_findings.body: `end` equals `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition can never detect a slot that overruns the working-hour boundary, and slots extending past the end of availability are accepted.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Boundary-overrunning slots pass the newly added working-hours validation, defeating its purpose.
validated_findings.impact: `end` equals `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition can never detect a slot that overruns the working-hour boundary, and slots extending past the end of availability are accepted.
validated_findings.root_cause: Copy-paste of the start-time expression when computing the slot end offset.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compute `const end = slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute();` (handling day rollover) so the slot end is compared against `workingHour.endTime`.
validated_findings.title: Slot end minute computed from slot start time in working-hours check
validated_findings.trigger: A slot starts shortly before the end of the host's working hours, e.g. a 60-minute event starting at 16:30 when working hours end at 17:00.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 142 shows `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` which is identical to line 141's `start` calculation. This is a copy-paste error; `end` should use `slotEndTime` to properly check if slot extends past working hours.

validated_findings.body: `find` matches the 14:00-16:00 range (slot ends before its start), so the function returns false and the slot inside the 09:00-11:00 range is removed from the schedule.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Legitimate slots are dropped whenever a date has multiple override ranges.
validated_findings.impact: `find` matches the 14:00-16:00 range (slot ends before its start), so the function returns false and the slot inside the 09:00-11:00 range is removed from the schedule.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new override logic uses `find` for "some range excludes the slot" rather than aggregating all same-day ranges before deciding.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Determine availability with a positive predicate: mark the day as overridden, then return true only if `dateOverrides.some(range => slot fits inside range)`; return false only when no same-day range contains the slot.
validated_findings.title: Date-override check rejects a slot that falls outside any one of several same-day overrides
validated_findings.trigger: A host creates two ranges for the same date override (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00) and a slot at 09:30 is evaluated.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This describes the same `find` with exclusion predicate issue as candidate 1, but for dateOverrides instead of workingHours. Lines 106-127 show similar logic where finding any override that excludes the slot returns false. However, this is a distinct code location from candidate 1 and describes date overrides specifically.

validated_findings.body: Two distinct Dayjs objects are never reference-equal, so this branch never executes; the intended "whole day blocked" short-circuit is dead code and the decision falls through to the subsequent range comparisons, which can classify the slot as available.
validated_findings.failure_mode: An intentionally added guard never triggers, silently changing availability semantics for zero-length overrides.
validated_findings.impact: Two distinct Dayjs objects are never reference-equal, so this branch never executes; the intended "whole day blocked" short-circuit is dead code and the decision falls through to the subsequent range comparisons, which can classify the slot as available.
validated_findings.root_cause: Object identity comparison used where a value/time comparison is required for Dayjs instances.
validated_findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === so the empty-override branch is dead
validated_findings.trigger: A date override marks the day as fully unavailable, producing an override whose start and end are the same instant.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 114 shows `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` comparing two Dayjs objects with `===`. Dayjs objects are never reference-equal; should use `.isSame()` method. This branch is dead code.

validated_findings.body: `dayjs(date.start)...format()` renders in the server's local timezone while `slotStartTime` is a UTC dayjs, so the two day strings disagree and the override is either ignored (slots not restricted) or applied to the wrong day.
validated_findings.evidence:
dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") ===
        slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")
validated_findings.failure_mode: Availability differs between deployments depending on the server TZ setting; tests running in UTC hide the defect.
validated_findings.impact: `dayjs(date.start)...format()` renders in the server's local timezone while `slotStartTime` is a UTC dayjs, so the two day strings disagree and the override is either ignored (slots not restricted) or applied to the wrong day.
validated_findings.root_cause: New code parses the override Date without `.utc()`, making the day key dependent on the host process timezone.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use `dayjs.utc(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` so both sides of the comparison are in UTC.
validated_findings.title: Override day matched using server-local formatting against a UTC slot day
validated_findings.trigger: The Node process runs with a non-UTC TZ (e.g. TZ=America/New_York) and an override starts near a day boundary in UTC.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 110-111 show `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` compared to `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. The `dayjs(date.start)` parses in local timezone while `slotStartTime` is UTC. This can cause day mismatch depending on server TZ.

validated_findings.body: `hour()`/`minute()` discard the day rollover, yielding startTime=1230 and endTime=30; buildSlots skips ranges where `start >= end`, so the override day shows no slots at all (or slots at the wrong clock time when both ends roll over).
validated_findings.evidence:
startTime:
          dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 +
          dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").minute(),
        endTime:
          dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 +
          dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").minute(),
validated_findings.failure_mode: Date overrides silently produce empty or misplaced availability for invitees in distant timezones.
validated_findings.impact: `hour()`/`minute()` discard the day rollover, yielding startTime=1230 and endTime=30; buildSlots skips ranges where `start >= end`, so the override day shows no slots at all (or slots at the wrong clock time when both ends roll over).
validated_findings.root_cause: The new invitee-offset adjustment is applied to a timestamp but then reduced to same-day minutes-since-midnight without handling day boundary crossings.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compute the shifted minutes as a signed offset from the invitee day start (e.g. diff in minutes against `startOfInviteeDay`) and clamp/split ranges that cross midnight instead of taking `hour()*60 + minute()`.
validated_findings.title: Timezone-shifted override loses day rollover, producing endTime before startTime
validated_findings.trigger: Organizer in Asia/Kolkata sets a date override 09:00-13:00 IST and the invitee views the page in America/Los_Angeles (offset difference about -12.5h), so the shifted start falls on the previous calendar day while the end stays on the same day.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 218-223 compute startTime/endTime using `hour() * 60 + minute()` after adding timezone offset. When offset causes day rollover (e.g., -12h offset), hour()/minute() wrap around, potentially yielding endTime < startTime which buildSlots skips at line 68.

validated_findings.body: `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the runtime's guessed timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed for the server/browser zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary wrong offset, showing overrides at incorrect times.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Silent timezone misalignment for callers that do not populate the new optional field.
validated_findings.impact: `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the runtime's guessed timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed for the server/browser zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary wrong offset, showing overrides at incorrect times.
validated_findings.root_cause: The added `timeZone` field on TimeRange is optional while the new offset computation assumes it is always provided.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Either make `timeZone` required on the override input consumed by getSlots, or default explicitly, e.g. `.tz(override.timeZone ?? organizerTimeZone)`.
validated_findings.title: Optional override timeZone dereferenced without fallback in getSlots
validated_findings.trigger: Any getSlots caller that passes `dateOverrides` built from `TimeRange` values without the newly added optional `timeZone` field (the type declares `timeZone?: string`), e.g. team availability components or future callers.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 212 shows `.tz(override.timeZone)` where `timeZone` is optional per the type definition (line 5 of schedule.d.ts shows `timeZone?: string`). When undefined, `.tz(undefined)` falls back to runtime guess, causing incorrect offset calculation.
